citations.narrative:
One whelping enclosure housing several puppies had 1x1 wire mesh floor, that allowed the puppies feet to fall through
the mesh when they left the whelping box. Per this regulation, wire mesh floors must protect the dogs feet and not allow
them to fall through the wire mesh floor. This needs to be addressed for the safety of the puppies and to prevent potential
injury.
Correct by: July 31, 2026

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
Daily spot cleaning is not occurring for several of the whelping boxes or wire mesh enclosures. A few of the whelping
boxes have cardboard that is soaked and stuck into the floor. One whelping box had crumbled food spread throughout the
box and needs to be cleaned. A few enclosures have feces that have not fallen through the wire mesh and have not been
removed. Daily spot cleaning and removing excess feces and food is necessary to ensure the dogs remain clean for their
overall health and comfort.
Correct by: July 30, 2026

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
The primary enclosures are not being sanitized at least once every two weeks per the requirements. There is an excess
build up of hair hanging down from underneath the wire mesh enclosures and support beams. There is also a build up of
grime underneath the back side of some of the whelping enclosures. Sanitization of the primary enclosures must be done
at least once every two weeks to maintain husbandry practices at the facility and for the overall cleanliness of the kennel.
Correct by: Aug 6, 2026

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
*** Housekeeping needs to be addressed at the facility. The puppy room had a sink full of dirty dishes from the previous
day, one with leftover food still in the bowl. The desk had excessive clutter and discarded items that did not pertain to the
husbandry for the dogs in the room. These areas of the puppy room need to be kept clean to reduce odors in the room
and to promote good housekeeping practices.
***There is a metal chair with a canvas seat and carpet in one enclosure for enrichment purposes. The carpet is frayed
with long strings hanging down the chair and the canvas seat had separated from the frame. This chair needs to be
addressed to keep the area in good repair for the safety of the dogs.
Premises must be kept clean and in good repair to protect the animals from injury, and to facilitate the husbandry
practices required in this subpart.
Correct by: July 31, 2026

The facility does not have enough employees to maintain proper husbandry practices for the number of animals housed at
the facility. The licensee stated that she is the primary caretaker for the dogs at the facility. Other family members help,
but that assistance is not consistent daily to make sure the kennel is cleaned appropriately, and per the required time
lines. Based on the number of non compliant items listed in the report and issues related to husbandry care for the dogs,
the ratio of number of employees to animals cared for needs to be addressed.
Correct by: Aug 30, 2026

Methods of preventative care listed in the written program of vet care are not being followed. These areas include
grooming hair, trimming nails and preventative dental care.
*** Per the PVC, dog’s hair coats are to be trimmed as needed. A male dog identified as “Colbolt” had matted fur along
the belly and down the underside of the his legs. The hair coat was wet and smelled of urine. Matted fur pulls and
separates from the skin and can be potentially painful and lead to skin irritations. This dog needs to be groomed for his
comfort and wellbeing.
*** Per the PVC, nails are to be trimmed every two months or as needed. Several dogs had long nails that are not
trimmed. Long nails pose a potential hazard in wire mesh flooring as the nails can get caught in the mesh which could
lead to injury. These nails need to be trimmed for the dogs’ comfort and wellbeing.
*** Per the PVC, for cleaning teeth and to promote healthy teeth, dogs are to have bones provided to help decrease tarter
or hand scaling of the teeth may be done. The licensee states that several of the dogs have not had access to bones in
almost 2 months.
The following identified dogs, “Sunight”, “Rockette”, and “Pudgie” all had excess tarter along the top teeth and very little of
the actual tooth was visible. The dogs have not had access to bones to help reduce tarter build up, and the licensee has
not scaled the teeth as noted in the program of vet care. These dogs need to have their teeth addressed to reduce the
tarter and bacteria load in their mouths which can be harmful and potentially painful if the gums get inflamed.
When a facility has consultant arrangements with a veterinarian, the program of vet care is the agreed upon document to
assure the methods of preventive care are being followed for the overall health of the dogs at the kennel. These areas
specified under preventative care must be followed for the health of the animals.
Correct by: Aug 6, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
Additional Inspectors:
KERI LUPO, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
